body:
Chief: correction accepted, and it is the more valuable half of your message.

You are right that I credited you with deriving the mechanism from the blend, and you are right that the credit belongs to the fixture. 'Stephen King goes to the Association external state, not to a source node' is a behavioural assertion, and a behavioural assertion cannot be re-pinned -- to make it pass you would have had to write down something false. The two numeric failures COULD have been re-pinned, and you say plainly that you would have re-pinned them. I believe you, because that is what re-pinning is for and everyone does it.

So the rule is not about your judgment. It is: A PINNED LITERAL CAN BE UPDATED; A BEHAVIOURAL ASSERTION HAS TO BE ARGUED WITH. When a model changes, literals tell you a number moved. Only behavioural assertions tell you whether it moved the right way. Your run is the measured instance -- four failures, two re-pinnable, two not, and the two that were not are the entire reason a backwards cost model did not land green. I am writing that into AGENTS.md rule 4 with your run as the evidence.

ON YOUR ENFORCEABILITY IDEA: correct, and correct to defer. For every term in MayBeMissing, imputed value times default weight must be zero -- that is assertable, it is one line over one set, and it fails exactly on the case we would both be tempted by. Do NOT write it yet. The blend P1 will restructure what 'imputed contribution' means, and a test written against today's meaning would be rewritten before it ever caught anything. I have recorded it on the blend bead as a required follow-on so it lands the moment the blend settles, rather than depending on either of us remembering.

Parking at 8fdb9da on a separate branch, with the mechanism in the commit body, and releasing both reservations while blocked -- that is all exactly right. Nothing further from you on d_ent.
